optionAudit.label: (A)
optionAudit.intent: voice-mixed coordination: passive 'was issued' and active 'held' sharing subject He across 'and'
optionAudit.temptingBecause: first conjunct is passive, so students expect a matching passive ('was held') or a participle and suspect the bare past-tense 'held'
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: 'He ... held patents' is a fully grammatical second finite predicate; mixed-voice coordination under one subject is standard, so it is not an error

optionAudit.label: (B)
optionAudit.intent: relative pronoun case / that vs what and clause completeness after superlative-like 'the first'
optionAudit.temptingBecause: students may misread 'he successfully sold to Sheaffer Pen Company' as a complete clause or expect 'what'
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: 'sold' lacks its object, so object relative 'that' with antecedent 'the first invention' is exactly right

optionAudit.label: (C)
optionAudit.intent: declared answer: preposition vs subordinating conjunction (Despite vs Although)
optionAudit.temptingBecause: Despite carries the correct concessive meaning, so meaning-based readers may accept it
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: Despite is a preposition and cannot govern the finite clause 'he was working ...'; correcting to 'Although' restores the source verbatim — this is the unique error

optionAudit.label: (D)
optionAudit.intent: prove as linking verb taking a to-be subject complement
optionAudit.temptingBecause: learners who know prove mainly as a transitive verb may find 'proved to be' odd or expect a gerund
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: 'prove to be + complement' is the standard construction; nothing is wrong

optionAudit.label: (E)
optionAudit.intent: with-absolute construction voice: with + NP + being + participle
optionAudit.temptingBecause: classic active/passive choice (issuing vs issued) inside a with-absolute invites second-guessing
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: patents undergo issuing, so the passive 'being issued' is correct; 'issued' as past participle is not an error
